app.settings.title: Statutory profile
app.settings.description: The regime every payroll is calculated against: jurisdictions with the schemes, rates, overtime rules and limits configured inside them, and the companies bound to each
app.settings.header_description: The regime payroll is calculated against, and the companies bound to one. Contribution rates, overtime rules and overtime limits are not catalogues — they are configured inside the jurisdiction that levies them, and rate bands inside the scheme they belong to. The pay catalogue lives under Pay components and per-person registrations under People. Every rule is effective-dated — end-date and insert a successor, never update in place.
app.settings.jurisdictions_description: Open a jurisdiction to configure everything it sets: the statutory schemes it levies (and the rate bands inside each), what overtime is worth, and the ceiling on overtime hours. None of those is a catalogue of its own.
app.settings.companies_description: The legal entities payroll runs for, each bound to the jurisdiction whose regime prices it.

component.payslips_description: Open a payslip for its direct component and statutory line breakdown.
component.component_breakdown_descriptio: Each row is the direct, queryable link from this payslip to its pay component, input entry, or statutory scheme.
component.consumed_inputs_description: The database-enforced source links this payslip priced. Each attendance or leave record can belong to one payslip only.
component.employments_description: One row per company this person works for. hire_date drives service months and every leave accrual.
component.contractual_terms_description: Effective-dated pay and classification for each engagement. End-date and insert a successor; never update in place.
component.statutory_registrations_descri: Where each engagement stands with each statutory scheme — registered with a reference, or not registered with a reason.
component.statutory_contributions_descri: The schemes this regime levies, in the order payroll applies them. Open one for the rate bands that price it — a band belongs to a scheme, not to the jurisdiction.
component.ordinary_pay_note: Ordinary pay is divided by {divisor} {unit} a month. Every rule here is effective-dated — end-date and insert a successor, never update in place.
component.rate_bands_description: One rung of this scheme's ladder: the selector that picks it — wage, wage and age, headcount or risk class — and the award it pays. A floor is the first band, a ceiling the terminal one.
component.create_run_hint: Creating the run builds it: the payslips and their complete component lines are written before this closes.
component.provision_remainder_hint: The remainder, if any, is placed on the final instalment so the total is exact.
component.risk_class_hint: The occupational risk group the entity is rated in, where its regime prices a contribution by risk. Indonesia's JKK is the one such scheme here: class {class_iv} is charged at 0.89% and class {class_i} at 0.24%, so an Indonesian entity left blank matches no band and its payroll run stops by name rather than quietly charging nothing. Malaysian and Philippine entities have no risk-keyed contribution and correctly leave this empty.
component.band_beyond_normal: Beyond normal hours: {from} h to {to} h
